overview.description: Bieten (German: 'Bidding' or 'Offering') is a highly unusual gambling game from the Austrian Tyrol played with a 33-card German-suited pack including the iconic WELI wild card. Each player receives only 3 cards, and points are scored for having the best Heart card, the best Leaf card, the best pair/triple, the best sequence, and winning the last trick. Players can 'Bieten' (bet) on any of these categories, escalating the stakes, or their opponents can concede the point. It is essentially a multi-dimensional bluffing game.
overview.originName: Bieten (Laubbieten, Lab bietn, Labbieten, Bayrischer Pocker)
overview.deck: 33-card German-suited pack (William Tell or Salzburg pattern), including the WELI

history.origins: Rooted deeply in the Austrian Tyrol and Bavarian card-game tradition. The WELI card is a hallmark of Tyrolean card games. Bieten draws on the same tradition as Watten and Schnapsen.
timeline: Present: Still played actively in Tyrol, Bavaria, and South Tyrol, especially in mountain communities.
history.evolution: The game's core innovation is its multi-point structure. Unlike most games where ONE thing wins, Bieten has FIVE simultaneous point categories, each bettable independently.
history.cultural: The WELI card is unique to this region. In Bieten, it acts as a wild card and can represent any card.

setup.deck: 33-card German-suited pack: A, K, Over (O), Under (U), 10, 9, 8, 7 in 4 suits (Hearts/Rot, Leaves/GrÃ¼n, Bells/Schellen, Acorns/Eichel) + WELI (special 6 of Bells wild card).
setup.dealing: Deal 3 cards to each player. No trump is established. No kitty.

rules.objective: Score the most points across 5 categories: Best Heart (Rot), Best Leaf (GrÃ¼n), Best Pair/Triple (Gleich), Best Sequence (Hanger), and the Last Trick (Spiel).
rules.gameplay: Starting with best hand, players may 'Bieten' (bet) on any category they wish to contest. Any opposing player can either: Concede (auto-lose the category, worth its base value) OR Call (match the bet, escalating the point value). At showdown, the best hand wins the doubled/escalated value.
keyRules: WELI is wild: its owner declares what card it represents.
A player may bet on a category they cannot possibly win as a bluff.
Game targets a fixed score (e.g., 15 points).

strategy.basic: Don't Bieten a category you can't win unless you're willing to bluff. With 3 cards, information is scarce.
strategy.intermediate: The WELI allows creative bluffs. If you hold WELI + a middling card, you can Bieten for Best Heart claiming your WELI is the Ace of Hearts. Opponents don't know!
strategy.advanced: Multi-Category Hands: A hand with a pair AND a high heart is extremely powerful. Bieten on multiple fronts forces opponents to spend concessions.
tips: Conceding is not weaknessâ€”if the bet is small and your card is weak, save your chips.
The Last Trick (Spiel) is a guaranteed category for the player holding the highest card in the last suit led.

difficulty.easy: Bets only on categories with real cards. Never bluffs.
difficulty.medium: Uses WELI wisely. Evaluates 2+ categories per hand.
difficulty.hard: Multi-category bluffer. Calculates opponent hand ranges from their bet/concede decisions. Manages chip stack vs. risk.

considerations: WELI declaration is a major logical branching point.
Bluff detection requires probabilistic opponent modeling.

wildcards.restrictions: When played must declare rank and suit; ranks below the real card it represents; cannot declare in a way that breaks follow-suit.

edgeCases.text: WELI cannot be declared in a way that would have broken follow-suit (e.g. if you had a heart and did not follow, WELI cannot later be declared a heart).
To bet on or hold a figure you must have that figure in your hand (e.g. at least one heart for Rot; pair or triple for Gleich).
A player one point from target (gespannt) may not initiate a bet or say three; may still hold another player's bet.

customActions.description: Dealer offers cut; cutter may steal 0–3 cards from top of pack. Dealer then deals 3 cards to each player (fewer to cutter if they stole). Undealt cards placed face up.
customActions.constraints: Dealer acts; cutter may take up to 3 cards from top of cut. Everyone ends with 3 cards.

customActions.description: Propose to raise a figure's value (e.g. from 1 to 2 points). Other players in turn say Gut (concede) or Halten (hold). If all concede, bettor wins 1 point; if any hold, figure is contested for 2 points. You may only bet on a figure you have in hand.
customActions.constraints: Must have the figure in hand to bet (e.g. at least one heart to bet on Rot). After first card of last trick, cannot bet on Spiel unless you have a card of the suit led.

customActions.description: Concede a figure to the bettor (say Gut) or hold the bet (say Ich halte) to contest for increased points. To hold you must have that figure in hand.
customActions.constraints: When responding to a bet, may say Gut (concede) or Halten (hold). To hold you must have the figure in your cards.

customActions.description: After the last trick, determine winner of each figure (Rot, Grün, Gleich, Hanger, Spiel) and award points based on betting outcome. Bet figures scored first in bet order, then unbet figures: Red, Green, Gleich, Hanger, Game.
customActions.constraints: System evaluates when all cards are face up after three tricks.

engine.handRankingSystem: Five figures: Rot (best heart), Grün (best leaf), Gleich (best pair or triple), Hanger (best sequence), Spiel (last trick). No poker hands.
engine.deckDescription: One standard 32-card deck plus one Weli (or joker) card: eight ranks (seven through ace) in each of four German suits, plus the Weli wild card. Used for Bieten (Tyrolean betting game) where the Weli can represent any card.
engine.suitDescription: Four German suits (acorns, leaves, hearts, bells). Each suit has eight cards; the Weli is a separate card that acts as wild. Trump and plain-suit order apply; the Weli is often the highest trump or a wild card.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit (seven through ace) plus the Weli. In Bieten, points are scored for best heart, best leaf, best pair or triple, best sequence, and last trick. The Weli counts as any card; standard 32-card point values apply otherwise.

synthesis.shortDescription: A rare bluffing masterpiece from the Austrian Alps. With only 3 cards, you compete on 5 distinct categories simultaneouslyâ€”and a single wild WELI card can win any of them. Bold betting is everything.

prompts.human: You hold the WELI, the King of Hearts, and the 9 of Bells. Bieten on 'Rot' (Best Heart) claiming the WELI is the Ace of Hearts! Your King alone is already competitive. If they call your bluff, you reveal the WELI truly is an Ace.
